verses.1: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go and speak to Pharaoh. Say to him, ‘As the LORD, the God of the Israelites, says: “Send away my people, so that they can worship me.”’”
verses.2: For if you are willing to send them away, yet still you hold them in your possession.
verses.3: Look! The hand of the LORD is in your fields, where there are horses, chariots, and people riding them, in the morning and at noon. It’s a time of great joy and celebration.
verses.4: And Jehovah brought down destruction between the people of Israel and the people of Egypt. But not a single person from the people of Israel died as a result.
verses.5: And the LORD said, “Afterward, the LORD will do this thing on earth.”
verses.6: And Jehovah did this from the evening time. All the people of Egypt and all the Israelites died; not one person survived.
verses.7: And Pharaoh sent out his people from Israel. But none of them died from their journey. This pleased Pharaoh, and he did not send the people away.
verses.8: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take some of the ointment from your clothes, mix it with water, and sprinkle it over Pharaoh’s eyes.”
verses.9: And it shall be a curse upon all the people of Egypt. It shall also be a curse upon man and beast, that they may not bear fruit in all the land of Egypt.
verses.10: And they took the incense from the altar, and stood before Pharaoh. Moses handed it over to Pharaoh. Then, white dust began to rise from the people and animals.
verses.11: And the priests were unable to stand before Moses, because the dirt was still on them and on all of the priests.
verses.12: And Jehovah strengthened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not listen to them, as Jehovah had commanded Moses.
verses.13: And the LORD said to Moses, “Stand in front of Pharaoh in the morning. Then say to him, ‘As the LORD, the God of the Israelites, says: “Send out my people and let them worship me.”’”
verses.14: For at this time I will send all my messengers to your heart, to your servants, and to your people. In doing so, you will know that there is no one like me in all the land.
verses.15: For now, I have sent my hand against you and your people through these words. You will be destroyed from this land.
verses.16: But in this regard, you stood forth in front of me, so that my power might be known throughout all the earth.
verses.17: Your name is still spoken among my people, so that I may not be able to send you away.
verses.18: I am now bringing forth a very beautiful fragrance from the garden. It’s something that has never existed in Egypt since its establishment until now.
verses.19: And now, send the fox away with your possessions and everything you have in the field. All the people and animals that are found in the field will die. The locusts will come and eat them all.
verses.20: He heard what the Lord said. He drove Pharaoh’s servants and their possessions into exile.
verses.21: And he did not pay attention to the words of the LORD. He abandoned his servants and his possessions in the field.
verses.22: And the LORD said to Moses, “Raise your hand over the land of Egypt. So there will be darkness over all the land of Egypt, on people, animals, and every plant that grows in Egypt.”
verses.23: And Moses raised his hand over the heavens. Then Jehovah sent fire down to the earth. The fire spread across the land of Egypt. Jehovah used fire to destroy the Egyptians.
verses.24: And there was fire and smoke inside the fire. It was a very intense fire. There was no such fire anywhere else in Egypt since that time when it became a nation.
verses.25: And the locusts covered all the land of Egypt. They ate up everything that was in the fields, from people to animals, and every kind of plant in the fields. The locusts destroyed all the trees in the fields.
verses.26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel lived, was there no plague.
verses.27: And Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron. He said to them, “I have sinned this time. May the LORD be merciful to me, and to my people who are sinners.”
verses.28: Entreat the LORD, for there is great wrath from God. I will send you away, and do not be afraid to stand up against Him.
verses.29: And Moses said to him, “When I leave this city, I will bow my head before Jehovah. May the noise and the clamor cease. Let there be no more of it, so that you may know that this land belongs to Jehovah.”
verses.30: And I know that you and your servants will not fear before the LORD God.
verses.31: And the wheat and the barley were destroyed, because barley represents spring, while wheat represents autumn.
verses.32: And the sheep and the lamb did not get up, because it was still dark.
verses.33: And Moses went out from Pharaoh’s presence, and he bowed his head before God. Then the noise and the clamor ceased, and no one was able to continue their attacks on the land.
verses.34: And Pharaoh saw that the plagues and disasters had stopped. He became complacent about his sins, and he began to enjoy himself with his servants.
verses.35: And Pharaoh’s heart became stubborn, and he did not send out the children of Israel as Jehovah had commanded through Moses.
